_comment: Om-curated annotation flags attached to taxa. They say a taxon is on a published list. They are not evidence that a sample carries resistance or disease: the presence or abundance of a taxon never implies resistance. Taxa may be genus, species, family or order scientific names; a flag on a clade applies to everything below it.

flags.label: WHO bacterial priority pathogen 2024, critical
flags.note: The list names resistant phenotypes (carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, third-generation cephalosporin-resistant and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis). Taxonomy alone cannot show resistance.

flags.label: WHO bacterial priority pathogen 2024, high
flags.note: Listed for specific resistant phenotypes (for example vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus). Taxonomy alone cannot show resistance.

flags.label: WHO bacterial priority pathogen 2024, medium
flags.note: Listed for specific resistant phenotypes. Taxonomy alone cannot show resistance.

flags.label: ESKAPE group
flags.note: Group of nosocomial pathogens that escape common antibiotics. Presence in a gut or skin profile is not a clinical finding.
